correctness.rationale: Direct per-petal classification gives three disjoint center-label regimes. With center 2, no more than one zero lacking a petal defender is possible; with center 1, the same petal cannot have two zeros and exactly one defender; with center 0, exclude precisely all ones and one defender plus one zero. These exactly yield the written polynomial. Initial degrees prove every homogeneous minimum and count, including the triangular two-petal correction. Direct adjacency-based finite tests check 215298 ternary assignments over ten configurations; an independent C++ counter checks seven homogeneous instances including q=3,s=4. Neither finite experiment substitutes for the stated unbounded proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison of actual statements, not only titles: Koch and Shank give definitions and general 2-attack extremal machinery, not this full bouquet coefficient polynomial or the sharp optimizer count. Readable proofs of ordinary, weak and total Roman weight enumerators on the identical clique-bouquet graph family use different predicates and admit configurations forbidden by simultaneous-attack defense. Targeted queries for the same invariant, its aliases, its graph-family aliases, and broader coefficient formulas found no implication. This assessment is provisional, not a global priority certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical enumeration might already give the identical two-attack bouquet coefficients.

value.rationale: The result completely enumerates a natural simultaneous-two-attack defense invariant over all heterogeneous clique bouquets. Its cross-petal constraint introduces a global correction absent from related Roman polynomials. In the homogeneous class it yields sharp distinct optimizer structures and counts for petal orders two, three and at least four, with a genuine two-triangle exception (63 optima). The exact distribution, not just the scalar minimum, is a motivated natural graph invariant.
